title: Review of c34's rod-made ring: replicates on fresh seed 3 and on seed 4 at half the world's own step (signed-distance ring test passed in 100% of body-frames, rim/core 2.67-2.77, rim/out 7.8-7.9; 25-26 persistent splits); no track swims 3 body lengths and then divides (best 1.69-1.88 labkit BL)
summary: c34's world (surfactant source ks [phi>0] only, chis 5), labkit packs: seed 3 at dt 0.05 and seed 4 at dt 0.025 (WORLD_P dt, 200 steps per frame), T=1000. c21's sd_individuals.py on channel s: 435 and 527 body-frames, 100% pass both rim/core and rim/out >= 1.5, medians 2.67/7.93 and 2.77/7.76. Bodies from noise divide: 25 and 26 persistent splits, generation 4, merges 11-16; tracks move up to 3.4 and 4.7 labkit body lengths. c34's swimdivide.py: 25-28 tracks end in a two-child split, none moved >= 3 labkit body lengths first (best 1.69 and 1.88). Reading world.py: s is produced only where phi > 0 and decays everywhere, so the rods make all of it; the adsorption drift is written against the body field, which RUBRIC L3's quasi-equilibrium clause allows when the individual makes the species.

observations.B: results.txt: 100% of body-frames pass the signed-distance ring test on seed 3 and seed 4 (dt/2); pack3/sheet.png: rods from noise with a pink surfactant rim

seeds_run.result: pass at world dt/2: ring 100%, 26 persistent splits, 0 swim-then-divide

verdicts.limitation: The ring is a quasi-equilibrium coating of a rod-made species; it does no work here (s does not act back on phi), as c34 says. I relied on c34's chis=0 ablation and did not rerun it. Swim-then-divide on the same individual is still absent on my two runs, so this gives B to the rods but not SIBMD.
